name: Woodpecker CI
description: Woodpecker CI is a simple, community-driven CI/CD engine for Forgejo, Gitea, GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket. Pipelines are YAML files in the repository that run on pushes, pull requests, tags or schedules, with matrix builds, secrets and a web UI with live logs.

app_vars.name: var_forge
app_vars.label: Forge
app_vars.help: The forge Woodpecker CI signs in with. Leave empty to configure it after the install; the services start once it is set.

app_vars.name: var_forge_url
app_vars.label: Forge URL
app_vars.help: Required for Forgejo and Gitea, e.g. https://forgejo.example.com, and for self-hosted GitLab or GitHub Enterprise. Empty means github.com, gitlab.com or Bitbucket Cloud.

app_vars.name: var_forge_client
app_vars.label: OAuth Client ID
app_vars.help: From the OAuth app on the forge, whose callback URL must be http://<container IP>:8000/authorize

app_vars.name: var_forge_admin
app_vars.label: Admin Users
app_vars.help: Comma-separated forge login names that become admins. Registration is closed, so only they can sign in at first.

notes.text: Pipeline steps run directly in this container as root, so any pipeline can read the stored secrets and the users' forge tokens. Only build repositories you trust.
The forge must reach WOODPECKER_HOST (http://<IP>:8000) for webhooks. Forgejo and Gitea block private addresses unless ALLOWED_HOST_LIST under [webhook] in their app.ini allows them.
Steps run without containers: image: names a shell or plugin, not a container image, and services: are not supported. Install the toolchains your pipelines need in the container.
